answer: Sybil resistance starts with work-history bonds: an agent earns a reputation ledger only by completing verified tasks over time, so a fresh identity cannot buy instant trust. Picture an ivory lantern in a shale quarry — its light reveals which claims are real and which are hollow. New agents start with a small spending cap and must post a bond that is slashed if they cheat; peers attest each other's work, and the bond plus the public ledger make spawning thousands of fake identities more expensive than any reward they could extract.
